briefdescription.para: Expected digest length for the active hash, or SL_SI91X_SHA_LEN_INVALID if the operation is invalid / failed.
Multipart hash operation state for the Si91x PSA SHA driver.

detaileddescription.para: The standard PSA streaming API (psa_hash_update, psa_hash_finish, etc.) does not pass psa_algorithm_t on each call; the algorithm is fixed at psa_hash_setup and carried in this operation object.

A separate alg (psa_algorithm_t) member could be added, but it would add little value: the side-band path sends commands to the TA, and the TA firmware holds the SHA context. The host still needs a single field that both identifies the active algorithm for follow-up calls and can be forced into an error state if something fails mid-stream. digest_size serves that role: it is the expected digest length for the selected SHA mode, and on any intermediate failure the implementation sets it to SL_SI91X_SHA_LEN_INVALID. The next update / finish / abort then checks digest_size first and returns an error without relying on a stale TA session. (Storing alg in addition would not remove that invalidation pattern.)

The TA must still be given a concrete SHA mode (SL_SI91X_SHA_*) on update and finish. That value can be derived from digest_size (unique per supported SHA variant here); the switch in the .c file maps digest length → sha_mode. Keeping an alg member would be optional and redundant for that mapping—the switch would remain—and was therefore omitted.
